text:
Alex K.: ok team — onboarding shadow for new on-call starts this weekend. want to lock down primary/secondary shifts, handoff pointers, and where to find quick mitigation steps if we get paged. I’ll post a short checklist below.

Morgan L.: I can take primary Sat 07:00-19:00 (PST). Taylor can be secondary unless anyone objects. Jamal can be backup for escalations after 17:00.

Taylor R.: good for me. I’ll be on call before the deploy so flag me if we see any latency spikes during the rollout.

incident-bot: page routed: PROD-API-LATENCY -> oncall@redwood (primary: Morgan L., secondary: Taylor R.). Alert threshold: p95 > 600ms for 5m.

Sophie P.: quick runbook pointers for the shadow — copy these into your notes: 
• Runbook: <https://internal.redwood/runbooks/prod-api-latency|PROD API Latency Runbook>
• Quick mitigation: 1) disable non-essential feature-flag (feature:heavy-acct-queries), 2) scale up serving pool for model-batches, 3) enable degraded-path fallback to small-model (model:rw-small-v2).

Alex K.: adding the small checklist we use for handoffs and paging: 
```
Handoff checklist:
- Confirm primary/secondary and post in thread
- Share active incidents + pager links
- Any ongoing mitigations or postmortems to note
- Short recap of last 12h deploys and config changes
- Shadow tasks: observe a page, run a simulated failover (if safe)
```

Morgan L.: we just rolled a minor quantization tweak at 05:30 — it increased CPU on the batching node but not token latency. I’ll keep an eye on batch sizes.

Jamal S.: noted — I'll set a conservative autoscale policy for the weekend: min 4 GPUs on critical pool, burst to 8. If we hit repeated OOMs escalate to infra.

Taylor R.: if paged, first quick triage plan I use: 1) check infra metrics (batch queue depth, gpu mem), 2) check inference runtimes per model, 3) run fallback to rw-small-v2 for the affected route, 4) notify customers via status if >30m impact.

Sophie P.: for the shadowing newbies: please observe a page and follow this 'safe mitigation' flow — we don't flip live knobs unless primary approves. Safe mitigation = feature-flag toggle, scale up, or switch to fallback model.

Alex K.: schedule for shadowing — @Taylor R. pair with @Sophie P. for the first 2 hours of your shift (07:00–09:00). then Sophie will hand off to Jamal at 09:00 for escalation coverage. Please confirm in thread and add calendar.

Morgan L.: confirmed. I'll DM the shadowing list with a quick note and the checklist.

incident-bot: note: recent customer impact summary (last 24h) — 3 degraded responses from EU region, all mitigated by fallback model. No outages.

Taylor R.: quick question — where do we record who did the handoff? I usually update the oncall sheet.

Alex K.: yes, update the oncall-sheet spreadsheet and drop a one-line summary in #eng-oncall with the timestamp. Example: "2026-03-14 09:00 UTC — handoff Morgan -> Taylor (shadow: Sophie) — no active incidents."

Sophie P.: adding runbook snippet for the shadow: 
- command to toggle flag: `curl -X POST https://ff.redwood/internal/toggle -d '{"flag":"heavy-acct-queries","state":"off"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN'`
- quickest check: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` and `grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/d/serve/latency-overview`

Jamal S.: all set from infra side. I left a note in the infra runbook about weekend conservative scaling.

Alex K.: thanks everyone. last ask: new shadowers, when you observe a real page, DM me a short postmortem note (what you saw, what you tried). that helps accelerate ramp. :thumbsup:

Taylor R.: will do. excited to get the shadowing started. :eyes:
